name: Stereolab
label: Drag City
lede: A band named after a hi-fi demonstration record, singing French Marxist-flavored pop over Farfisa drones, that sold a few hundred thousand records without ever pretending to be a rock band.

eras.title: A Paris gig and a McCarthy breakup
eras.text: Tim Gane spent the late 1980s in McCarthy, a sharp, funny indie-pop band from Barking with left-wing lyrics. A McCarthy show in Paris is where he met Lætitia Sadier, and when McCarthy ended in 1990 the two had the start of a new band.

years.h: Tim Gane co-founds McCarthy in Barking, east London
years.p: McCarthy make jangly, politically pointed indie pop through the late 1980s, with Tim Gane on guitar.

years.h: Tim Gane meets Lætitia Sadier at a McCarthy gig in Paris
years.p: Lætitia Sadier, a Parisian, meets Tim Gane at a McCarthy concert in Paris. The two become a couple for the next 14 years.

years.h: Lætitia Sadier sings on McCarthy's last album
years.p: McCarthy's final album, Banking, Violence and the Inner Life Today, has Lætitia Sadier on it. Then McCarthy folds, softly by Tim Gane's account.
years.xp:
Gane told Chickfactor that McCarthy was mostly funny and fun and ended very softly, with no big blow-up.

Out of the wreckage came Stereolab: Gane and Sadier with Martin Kean on bass (ex-[[The Chills|90b5813d-fbd7-4539-89d5-034094f64a2e]]), Joe Dilworth on drums (from [[Th' Faith Healers|d9c7e489-54c0-413b-b7a5-4af14a2fd305]]) and Gina Morris on backing vocals.

years.h: Stereolab takes its name from a Vanguard hi-fi test series
years.p: Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier name the new band after Stereolab, the hi-fi demonstration division of Vanguard Records.

eras.title: Their own label, their own sound
eras.text: Stereolab started its own label, Duophonic, before it had a record to put on it, and built a following on limited singles and EPs. Mary Hansen and Andy Ramsay arrived, and by 1993 an American major, Elektra, was paying for the records while Duophonic kept the UK.

years.h: Super 45: Stereolab's first record, and Duophonic's first too
years.p: An EP on the band's own Duophonic label, the first release for both the band and the label.

years.h: Mary Hansen and Andy Ramsay join Stereolab
years.p: Australian singer and guitarist Mary Hansen, who had known Tim Gane since McCarthy days, joins on second voice and guitar. Andy Ramsay takes over the drums and Duncan Brown the bass.

years.h: Peng!, Stereolab's first album, on Too Pure
years.p: Stereolab's debut LP comes out on London's Too Pure, motorik drone under Lætitia Sadier's cool French-accented singing.

q: We're too polite to demand anything, although we always ask for cider.
years.h: Switched On gathers the early singles
years.p: Too Pure in the UK and Slumberland Records in the US collect Stereolab's sold-out early singles on Switched On.
years.xp: Gane told Chickfactor the band chased the Slumberland single because not much was happening for Stereolab in America and it might get them noticed. It worked, though the colored vinyl sleeve they planned never got made.

years.h: Katharine Gifford and Sean O'Hagan join on keys and guitar
years.p: Katharine Gifford comes in on keyboards and [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]] leader Sean O'Hagan joins on guitar and keys for a spell.

years.h: Space Age Bachelor Pad Music gets Elektra calling
years.p: A mini-album of lounge-exotica pastiche on Too Pure. It raised Stereolab's profile enough to land an American deal with Elektra Records.

years.cap: Duophonic in the UK, Elektra in the US
years.h: Transient Random-Noise Bursts: an Elektra album, on Duophonic
years.p: Stereolab's second album comes out on Elektra in America while Duophonic keeps the UK release, a split they held for the next decade.
years.xp: The deal was unusual for a major: Stereolab kept their own label at home and handed Elektra the US. Duophonic stayed the band's base for everything they released after.

eras.title: Marx on the charts, Lollapalooza in a van
eras.text: A charting single and a Marx-quoting pop song put Stereolab in the music press and on American summer festival bills. The line-up kept shifting, but the Gane and Sadier core held.

years.h: "Jenny Ondioline" gives Stereolab its first UK chart entry
years.p: The Jenny Ondioline EP enters the UK Singles Chart at number 75. Stereolab couldn't afford to press enough copies to meet demand.

years.h: Mars Audiac Quintet and the Marxist pop single "Ping Pong"
years.p: Stereolab's third album carries "Ping Pong", a bright pop tune whose lyric explains capitalism's boom-and-bust cycles.

q: None of us are Marxists. I've never even read Marx.
years.h: Tim Gane: Stereolab aren't actually Marxists
years.p: "Ping Pong" made Stereolab the Marxist band in the press. Tim Gane pushed back: none of them were Marxists, he said.
years.xp: The lyrics, mostly Lætitia Sadier's, leaned on Guy Debord's The Society of the Spectacle and the Situationists and Surrealists rather than party politics. Sadier's side project, Monade, is named for an idea from the philosopher Cornelius Castoriadis.

years.h: Sean O'Hagan steps back to guest status
years.p: After Mars Audiac Quintet Sean O'Hagan leaves as a full member to focus on [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]], though he keeps turning up on Stereolab records.

years.h: Refried Ectoplasm comes out in America on Drag City
years.p: The second Switched On singles collection is issued by Duophonic and, in the US, Drag City, starting Stereolab's run with the Chicago label.

years.h: Stereolab play the Lollapalooza second stage
years.p: Stereolab tour America on the 1995 Lollapalooza second stage, the same summer [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] were on the main bill.

years.h: Morgane Lhote has to learn 30 songs to join
years.p: Katharine Gifford leaves and Duncan Brown goes too. New keyboardist Morgane Lhote is told to learn 30 songs before she's in; Richard Harrison takes the bass.

eras.title: Chicago loops
eras.text: Working with John McEntire of Tortoise in Chicago, Stereolab traded drone for loops, vibraphone and horns, and made the records most fans put first. By the end of the decade they'd sold a reported 300,000 albums in America.

years.h: Emperor Tomato Ketchup, cut in London and Chicago with John McEntire
years.p: Stereolab's fourth album, recorded at Blackwing in London and Idful in Chicago with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], named after a Shūji Terayama film.
years.xp:
Tim Gane said the new loop-based sound came out of being stuck: working on a cover of [[The Godz|d01198aa-b733-4816-9393-cd0cb915db37]]' "ABC", he lifted four looped notes that became an early version of "Percolator".

Duophonic released it in the UK on March 18 and Elektra in the US on April 9. By August 1997 it had sold over 46,000 copies in America, mostly on college radio's back.

years.h: Dots and Loops reaches the Billboard 200
years.p: Stereolab's first album to chart in America, peaking at number 111, with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and [[Mouse on Mars|4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce]]' Jan St. Werner on board.

years.h: Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier have a child; Stereolab stops touring
years.p: After a seven-month tour, Stereolab takes a break when Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier's child is born.

years.h: Aluminum Tunes, the third Switched On, on Drag City
years.p: A double-disc roundup of singles and rarities, issued by Duophonic and Drag City.

years.h: Cobra and Phases: Jim O'Rourke and John McEntire co-produce
years.p: Stereolab's sixth album, co-produced by [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], got mixed reviews and peaked at 154 in America. Simon Johns is now on bass.
years.xp: By August 1999, according to Wikipedia's sources, Stereolab's US album sales had reached 300,000 copies.

eras.title: Losing Mary Hansen
eras.text: The band built a studio in France and made a warmer record, then lost the most in one year: Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier split as a couple, and Mary Hansen was killed on her bike in London. Stereolab kept going, and made the next album for her.

years.h: Sound-Dust wins critics back after Cobra and Phases
years.p: [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] produce again. Critics liked Sound-Dust more than Cobra and Phases.

years.h: Stereolab builds a studio north of Bordeaux
years.p: Stereolab start building their own studio in the French countryside north of Bordeaux. The same year Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier end their 14-year relationship.

years.h: Mary Hansen is killed by a lorry while cycling in London
years.p: Mary Hansen, Stereolab's second voice and guitarist since 1992, was hit by a lorry while riding her bicycle in London. She was 36.
years.xp:
The band's statement said the suddenness of her death had shocked them, and called her a special person. Hansen was born in Maryborough, Queensland, and also sang with [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]], [[Mouse on Mars|4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce]], Moonshake and Brokeback, and fronted her own band, Schema.

A 2004 EP, Hybird, collected her own music and artwork, with one track finished by Andy Ramsay.

years.h: Instant 0 in the Universe: the first Stereolab record since Mary Hansen's death
years.p: An EP recorded at the band's new studio in France.

years.h: Margerine Eclipse is dedicated to Mary Hansen
years.p: Stereolab's eighth album closes the Elektra years. The song "Feel and Triple" is Lætitia Sadier's tribute to Mary Hansen.
years.xp: It was the band's last album on Elektra, which was folded that same year.

eras.title: One album for 4AD, then a pause
eras.text: Without a major label, Stereolab put out a run of limited singles (collected as Fab Four Suture in 2006) and made a brisk pop record for 4AD. Then the manager announced a break that lasted a decade.

years.h: Chemical Chords, Stereolab's one album for 4AD
years.p: Short, horn-lit pop songs issued by Duophonic with 4AD.

years.h: Manager Martin Pike puts Stereolab on hiatus
years.p: Stereolab's manager announces an indefinite break so the members can work on other projects.

years.h: Not Music empties the Chemical Chords vaults
years.p: Leftover songs from the Chemical Chords sessions come out as Stereolab's last album for 15 years.

eras.title: The reissues bring them back
eras.text: A reissue deal with Warp Records got the band back on stage after ten years, and six years later came a new album nobody had quite expected.

years.h: Stereolab announce reissues on Warp and their first tour since 2009
years.p: Expanded, remastered versions of the albums start coming out through Duophonic and Warp.

years.cap: Stereolab at the Roundhouse, London, 2021 · Wikimedia
years.h: Stereolab's first show in ten years, at Primavera Sound Barcelona
years.p: Tim Gane, Lætitia Sadier and Andy Ramsay lead Stereolab back onstage at Primavera Sound in Barcelona, then play Primavera Porto the following weekend.

years.h: Unsolicited Stereolab packages arrive, 16 years to the day
years.p: Fans got packages of "unsolicited Stereolab material" containing a new song, exactly 16 years after the hiatus announcement.
years.xp: Newsletter subscribers got a word-search puzzle and posters went up in cities around the world. The official announcement came on April 8.

years.h: Instant Holograms on Metal Film, the first new album in 15 years
years.p: Tim Gane and Lætitia Sadier with Andy Ramsay, Joe Watson and Xavi Muñoz, plus [[Bitchin Bajas|6243b9cb-63ad-438d-88f9-50c35d3f1088]]' Cooper Crain and Rob Frye. It reached number 29 in the UK.
